{{Short description|British/Canadian particle physicist}}
'''James Lewis Pinfold''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|ARCS}} {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} (born 1950 in [[Ealing]], [[West London]]) is a British-Canadian physicist, specializing in [[particle physics]].

==Education and career==
Pinfold graduated in physics in 1972 with a B.Sc. from [[Imperial College London]] and in 1977 with a Ph.D. from the [[University of London]]. His Ph.D. thesis was on [[Neutral current|weak neutral currents]], stemming from his work as part of the [[Gargamelle]] discovery team. From 1977 to 1989, he held research assistant and senior research assistant positions at [[CERN]] (near [[Geneva]]) and [[Fermilab]] (near [[Chicago]]). From 1989 to 1992, he was an associate professor at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]]. At the [[University of Alberta]], he was from 1992 to 1996 an associate professor and from 1996 to 2016 a full professor, and he is since 2016 a distinguished university professor. From 1995 to 2004 he was the University of Alberta's Centre for Subatomic Research<ref name=UAlberta>{{cite web|title=James Pinfold, PhD, FRSC|website=University of Alberta, Directory|url=https://apps.ualberta.ca/directory/person/jpinfold|access-date=6 October 2022}}</ref> (renamed in 2006 the Centre for Particle Physics).<ref>{{cite web|title=Arthur B. McDonald Canadian Astroparticle Physics Research Institute|website=University of Alberta|url=https://mcdonaldinstitute.ca/network/affiliate-universities/university-of-alberta/|access-date=6 October 2022}}</ref> Since 2005 he has held a visiting professorship at [[King's College London]].<ref name=UAlberta/> He frequently travels back and forth between the University of Alberta and CERN in Geneva.<ref name=Sarkonak>{{cite news|newspaper=The Gateway: The University of Alberta's Official Student Newspaper|title=Decorated physics prof seeks to answer "the big questions"|last=Sarkonak|first=Jamie|date=6 October 2015|url=https://thegatewayonline.ca/2015/10/decorated-physics-prof-seeks-to-answer-the-big-questions/|access-date=6 October 2022}}</ref> He is the author or co-author of over 1250 citable publications and has given over 220 invited talks.<ref name=UAlberta/>

Pinfold was from 1988 to 1989 the spokesperson for [[List of Super Proton Synchrotron experiments|CERN's WA88 experiment]]. From 1987 to 1992 he was the spokesperson for the MODAL experiment at CERN's [[Large Electron Positron Collider]] (LEP).<ref name=UAlberta/> He was one of the founders in the 1990s of the [[ATLAS experiment]] involved in the [[Large Hadron Collider]] (LHC) discovery of the [[Higgs boson]].<ref name=KillamPrize>{{cite web|author=Brown, Michael|date=9 May 2018|title=Relentless quest to solve universe's puzzles lands U of A physicist major Killam Prize|website=University of Alberta|url=https://www.ualberta.ca/folio/2018/05/relentless-quest-to-solve-universes-puzzles-lands-u-of-a-physicist-major-killam-prize.html|access-date=6 October 2022}}</ref> From 2000 to 2002 he was the deputy spokesperson for ATLAS-Canada. Since 2000 he is the leader and spokesperson for the [[MoEDAL experiment]].<ref name=UAlberta/><ref name=Sarkonak/> From 2004 to 2010 he was the deputy co-spokesperson for the SLIM experiment.<ref name=UAlberta/><ref>{{cite arXiv|year=2006|last1=Balestra|first1=S.|last2=Cecchini|first2=S.|last3=Fabbri|first3=F.|last4=Giacomelli|first4=G.|last5=Giacomelli|first5=R.|last6=Giorgini|first6=M.|last7=Kumar|first7=A.|last8=Manzoor|first8=S.|last9=McDonald|first9=J.|last10=Margiotta|first10=A.|last11=Medinaceli|first11=E.|last12=Nogales|first12=J.|last13=Patrizii|first13=L.|last14=Popa|first14=V.|last15=Quereshi|first15=I.|last16=Saavedra|first16=O.|last17=Sher|first17=G.|last18=Shahzad|first18=M.|last19=Spurio|first19=M.|last20=Ticona|first20=R.|last21=Togo|first21=V.|last22=Velarde|first22=A.|last23=Zanini|first23=A.|title=Rare Particle Searches with the high altitude SLIM experiment|eprint=hep-ex/0602036}}</ref>

In 2007, he won an award from ASTech (Alberta Science & Technology Leadership Foundation) for his leadership in starting the Alberta Large-area Time-coincidence Array, or ALTA, Project. This educational and research project "involves spreading out many cosmic-ray detectors over vast areas, connecting them through the Internet, and synchronising their readings with an integrated GPS system. Most of the detectors are run by high school students".<ref>{{cite web|last=Chowdhury|first=Jeeshan|title=The ALTA Project, Dr. James Pinfold, U Of A; 2007 Winner: ASTech Award for Excellence In Science And Technology Public Awareness|website=ASTech Foundation|url=https://www.astech.ca/archives/indexofpastwinners/the-alta-project-dr-james-pinfold-u-of-a|access-date=6 October 2022}}</ref> In 2013 he was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada (RSC).<ref name=RSC>{{cite web|title=Four UAlberta faculty members named to Royal Society|date=6 September 2013|website=University of Alberta|url=https://www.ualberta.ca/folio/2013/09/four-ualberta-faculty-members-named-to-royal-society.html|access-date=6 October 2022}}</ref> In 2025, he was a recipient of the [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]] as a member of the ATLAS Collaboration.<ref>{{cite web|title=The 2025 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics awarded to ALICE, ATLAS, CMS and LHCb Collaborations|website=INFN Padova|date=10 April 2025 |url=https://www.pd.infn.it/eng/the-2025-breakthrough-prize-in-fundamental-physics-awarded-to-alice-atlas-cms-and-lhcb-collaborations/|access-date=16 July 2025}}</ref>
